brief: Goldman's daily digest leads with two think-pieces. First: a framework sizing AI-economy revenue needed for hyperscalers to earn 15% ROIC on Phase 2 AI capex; at $42bn/GW and 57GW of deployments by 2028, the six major hyperscalers need $1.42tn in CY2028-30 revenue ($11.6bn/GW annually); near-term ROIC compression is expected but not read as structurally poor economics, with attractive medium-to-long-term results forecast. Second: agentic AI commerce is framed as a long-duration transition catalyzing eCommerce adoption, shifting ad monetization and creating demand for transaction, payment and fraud infrastructure; Meta, Alphabet, Amazon, Visa, Mastercard, Equifax, TransUnion, Fair Isaac, Live Nation, Shopify, Cloudflare, StubHub, Walmart, SharkNinja and Tapestry are named beneficiaries. On Meta specifically: Connect 2026 signaled a shift to smart glasses as the primary AI interface, read as evidence of productizing compute; near-term milestones are Muse adoption and third-party commerce, not monetization (Buy, $725 TP). Remaining sections report single-stock calls: Hon Hai, Murata and Lasertec (all Conviction List Buys) on AI-server, MLCC and EUV demand; Rohto, Furukawa, JPX guidance raises; Yaskawa and Fanuc TP cuts on ERP/supply issues; China bank TP hikes ex Huaxia; five Asia healthcare CDMO names; and lower USD/JPY forecasts on BOJ tightening.
